keywords: Malayan Red Dwarf x Baybay Tall
excerpt: PCA 15 3 is a registered coconut variety, also sold or known as Malayan Red Dwarf x Baybay Tall or MRD x BAYT. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1996 as NSIC 1996 Co 03. Its record notes 1.88 tonnes of copra per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

Its average yield of 1.88 t copra/ha matches the average of its group, 1.85. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

blocks.text: The pests and diseases that hit coconut fields most often: [coconut bud rot](/diseases/coconut-bud-rot), [coconut cadang cadang](/diseases/cadang-cadang), [coconut leaf beetle (Brontispa)](/pests/coconut-leaf-beetle), [coconut rhinoceros beetle](/pests/coconut-rhinoceros-beetle), [coconut scale insect (cocolisap)](/pests/cocolisap). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its fruiting season is 12, bearing regular. Each palm gave about 71.2 nuts a year in the records, with 249.3 grams of copra per nut.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** About 71 nuts per palm a year, 2.76 t copra/ha.
**Uses:** Copra, virgin coconut oil, coconut sap sugar.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: ranked above PCA 15 1 on productivity and profit in a PCA review, recommended for both VCO and sap sugar. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant PCA 15 3 coconut

Talls live long and stand typhoons, dwarfs bear early and are easy to harvest, and hybrids between the two give the most copra. Pick by use: copra, buko, or both. Get seednuts from a PCA accredited source. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for tree crops](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Malayan Red Dwarf x Baybay Tall the same as PCA 15 3?
items.a: Yes. Malayan Red Dwarf x Baybay Tall is another name for PCA 15 3, registered as NSIC 1996 Co 03. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows 1.88 tonnes of copra per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of PCA 15 3?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
